title: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary failings revealed in damning report

evidence_packet.title: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary failings revealed in damning report
evidence_packet.lead: The Wigan hospital had one of the country's worst record for A&E waits
evidence_packet.summary: The Wigan hospital had one of the country's worst record for A&E waits
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary failings revealed in damning report - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary's urgent and emergency care and medical care had been previously rated as "good" by inspectors By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 2 hours ago Records show a hospital trust is "among the worst in England" for people spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department. More than 900 people faced stays of such length in the month prior to a damning inspection. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has downgraded urgent and emergency care at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan, Greater Manchester, after several concerns were raised over patient care. A warning notice has been issued over the triage system, the identification of sepsis and how those with mental health needs are cared for after the unannounced inspection in May, with "rapid improvements" called for. The trust said it was "working hard" to make improvements. The NHS watchdog previously rated the urgent and emergency care and the medical care at the hospital - which was also inspected - as "good" but has downgraded them both to "requires improvement". Inspectors said the service was not meeting any of its sepsis targets citing two cases where staff had identified potential sepsis and follow up actions had not been completed more than 18 hours later. National guidelines state they should be done within an hour. Inspectors found leaders had not ensured there were dedicated spaces to safely accommodate high-risk young people with mental health needs, with some staff saying they had experienced physical and psychological harm as a result. Inspectors said the physical limitations of the department meant staff could not always respect people's dignity and privacy

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother who shook her two-year-old daughter to death will not have her nine-year sentence increased after Court of Appeal judges ruled it was not "unduly lenient" Morsal Mohammed Naim, 33, of Levenshulme, admitted manslaughter and child cruelty after her daughter, Omra Wali Jan, suffered a catastrophic brain injury and later died The Attorney General referred the sentence imposed at Manchester Crown Court in February. The animal welfare charity is proposing to create what it describes as a "one-stop shop" from rescue to recovery for animals most in need on farmland close to Pennington Flash in Leigh, Wigan. The charity said up to 150 jobs would be based at the Mossley Hall site if approved. It has submitted a environmental impact assessment report, published on Wigan Council's planning portal, which has been commissioned ahead of a full planning application. The document states that an "integrated animal welfare, veterinary, rehabilitation and education campus" is proposed on land at Mossley Hall on Slag Lane, Lowton, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. Part of the site is just 50 metres (164 ft) away from the Pennington Flash nature reserve. The 15 hectare site is made up of agricultural land, a disused railway embankment and woodland. The document said the development would include clinical veterinary and behavioural facilities, rehabilitation, training and rehoming provision and administration buildings. The report said: "The main building with veterinary services and staff offices, a ferret block and an electrical substation will be located in the central south of the site. "The campus will include a small animals block, a hay barn, cattery blocks and a foul drainage treatment plant." The Simister Island junction of the M60 Manchester Outer Ring Road will be closed - and the motorway shut in both directions to junction 17 (Whitefield) - on the weekends of 26 September and 10 October, National Highways said. The removal will mark the completion of the current phase of the £207-£340m upgrade of Simister Island to ease congestion. The upcoming weekend closures are as follows: 26-28 September: M60 anticlockwise (westbound): closed from 20:00 BST Saturday to 6:00 Monday M60 clockwise (eastbound): closed from 22:00 BST Saturday to 6:00 Monday 10-12 October: M60 anticlockwise (westbound): closed from 22:00 BST Saturday to 6:00 Monday M60 clockwise (eastbound): closed from 23.59 BST Saturday to 6:00 Monday The weekends were carefully chosen to reduce the impact on road users as much as possible, said National Highways. However, severe delays to journeys are expected, so motorists have been urged to plan ahead and avoid, where possible, the M60 between junctions 17 and 18 during the closures. Part of Alan Turing Way in east Manchester was closed in March and there are no signs of it reopening any time soon. The northbound section of the road between Ashton Old Road and Grey Mare Lane has been coned off with Manchester City Council conducting investigative works that are yet to be completed. Newton Heath resident David Carey said he tries to avoid using the route during rush hours and even when he uses it in off-peak hours to visit family, a 20-minute journey takes more than an hour. The council said it was taking time to ensure public safety and called for patience. It is expected the work to fix the sinkhole would take a considerable amount of time, given its size, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) said. Carey said the traffic lights to get towards the junction where you can get to the diversions causes a large tailback. The 59-year-old Manchester City supporter said with the football season restarting, traffic around the Etihad Stadium will become unbearable at weekends, as well as weekdays. He added: "It's getting darker and we are diverting traffic to get around this. The potential for a road traffic accident increases significantly." evidence_packet.evidence_text: The RSPCA's plans to build a regional animal welfare and rehabilitation campus have come a step closer The animal welfare charity is proposing to create what it describes as a "one-stop shop" from rescue to recovery for animals most in need on farmland close to Pennington Flash in Leigh, Wigan The charity said up to 150 jobs would be based at the Mossley Hall site if approved It has submitted a environmental impact assessment report, published on Wigan Council's planning portal, which has been commissioned ahead of a full planning application The document states that an "integrated animal welfare, veterinary, rehabilitation and education campus" is proposed on land at Mossley Hall on Slag Lane, Lowton, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said Part of the site is just 50 metres (164 ft) away from the Pennington Flash nature reserve

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over the years it has played host to The Smiths, Oasis and X-Factor auditions, but now the former G-Mex centre in Manchester is reportedly in the running to host Donald Trump and other world leaders The Manchester Central Convention Complex has been floated to be the venue for the G20, an annual gathering of the biggest economies from across the globe, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said If the city is chosen to host the event, the G20 would be the largest summit ever held in Manchester The government refused to confirm the details of the event, but insisted more information "will be announced in due course" The move to host the G20 in Manchester was reportedly set up months ago, after Andy Burnham became Prime Minister He used his first phone call with Trump to invite him to the city, which is said to have been accepted by the US president

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A leaderless council facing the threat of government intervention could finally end weeks of political deadlock Oldham councillors will vote on Wednesday on proposals to split responsibilities across political groups It follows a series of failed attempts to form an administration after no party won an overall majority at May's local elections The council has been operating without a political leader for six weeks after negotiations between political groups failed to produce an administration Oldham Council chief executive, Shelley Kipling, said: "The proposals being considered represent a strengthening of the governance arrangements already in place "They provide greater transparency, stronger democratic oversight and clear political engagement, while ensuring decisions can continue to be taken effectively and in the best interests of Oldham."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport bosses are warning of severe delays as a busy interchange and stretch of motorway is set to be closed for two weekends The Simister Island junction of the M60 Manchester Outer Ring Road will be closed - and the motorway shut in both directions to junction 17 (Whitefield) - on the weekends of 26 September and 10 October, National Highways said Simister Island, north of Manchester, connects the M60, M62, and M66 National Highways added the reason for the closure was to remove five overhead gantries that carried M60 signage, and together weighed about 450 tonnes. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A sinkhole has halted traffic in a busy area of Manchester causing months of frustration for residents and commuters Part of Alan Turing Way in east Manchester was closed in March and there are no signs of it reopening any time soon The northbound section of the road between Ashton Old Road and Grey Mare Lane has been coned off with Manchester City Council conducting investigative works that are yet to be completed Newton Heath resident David Carey said he tries to avoid using the route during rush hours and even when he uses it in off-peak hours to visit family, a 20-minute journey takes more than an hour The council said it was taking time to ensure public safety and called for patience It is expected the work to fix the sinkhole would take a considerable amount of time, given its size, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man convicted of murdering his millionaire fiancee in France has been jailed for a "degrading" attack on his elderly father Ian Griffin, 57, was living in the summerhouse of his parent's home in Winwick, Warrington, when police were called and found his father Bernard Griffin with serious facial injuries, Liverpool Crown Court heard In May 2009, he had been sentenced to 20 years in Paris for killing Kinga Legg, whose battered body was found in their room at the Bristol Hotel, but was released in 2016 after serving 22 months following an appeal on medical grounds The 57-year-old has been jailed for five years for causing grievous bodily harm and threatening to damage property Part of the attack, which was believed to have lasted between 30 minutes and an hour, was filmed by Griffin on his mother's phone It showed the defendant threatening his father to make him sign a note promising him to give 50% of his estate to his mother, Janet Griffin

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A pub dog helped uncover a trophy which disappeared during the Black Pudding Throwing Championships after she began sniffing around a seat where it had been left among toilet rolls Daisy, a Jack Russell-Chihuahua cross, caught the attention of The Oaks landlady Jessica Murray on Monday evening at the Ramsbottom pub When Murray investigated, she found the missing cup in a storage alcove beneath a lift-up seat, alongside toilet rolls kept there Organiser Paul Jenkins told BBC Radio Lancashire Breakfast the trophy had been located late on Monday "What better place to stash such an important historical piece of plasticky tin," he joked The trophy had disappeared from the presentation table during Sunday's competition, meaning organisers could not hold the usual trophy-lifting moment at the end of the event

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Celebrations for the official Black Pudding Throwing Championships were "subdued" after the trophy went missing during the event, organisers have said June Weir, 73, from Wilpshire, Lancashire, won the annual event at The Oaks pub in Ramsbottom, Bury, on Sunday, becoming the first female champion in its 100-year history Organiser Paul Jenkins said the presentation "lacked its sparkle" after the trophy disappeared from the prize table between 11:40 and 13:30 BST Now, he is appealing for whoever took it to return it, "with no questions asked" Jenkins said although the plastic cup was not worth a lot in monetary value, its disappearance had "hit a nerve" with the community as it was named after Phil Taylor - a long-time organiser of the competition who died last year aged 73 The quirky sporting event, which has been running for more than a century and raises money for charity, sees throwers hurl black puddings at Yorkshire puddings

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man accused of fatally stabbing an unwanted guest outside his on-off girlfriend's home told police he slipped while holding the knife due to running in socks, a court heard John Robinson is on trial at Bradford Crown Court accused of killing Mason Jones, following a confrontation in Burley in Wharfedale in March Prosecutor David Outterside said the 30-year-old had deliberately stabbed Jones, who was said to be unarmed, in the abdomen with a personalised Japanese chef's knife he brought to his ex's home Robinson, of Derry Hill in Menston, denies murder, manslaughter and possessing a blade in public Opening the case for the prosecution, the barrister said that Robinson told police officers during interview after his arrest that he was trying defend his ex-partner, Annabelle Ramsey, when Jones was stabbed Outterside said Robinson told police that Jones had hold of Ramsey, 23, around the neck after a confrontation and that he was trying to protect her

title: The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines

evidence_packet.title: The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhou
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:06, 16 Sep 2026 A notorious Manchester city centre street dubbed a council parking 'cash cow' has earned the town hall up to £724,000 in just three years even though there are only 29 bays, according to new figures obtained by the M For years St John Street in the city centre, home to a number of law chambers, was used by people heading into town to park for free after 8pm. All that changed in January 2024 when a new, single yellow line was painted along the road, prohibiting parking between 8pm and 8am In just three years, 22,607 penalty charge notices (PCNs) have been dished out to motorists caught out by the new arrangements, resulting in fines totalling £733,960, according to the new figures View 5 Images St John Street, Manchester (Image: Manchester Evening News) It means St John Street is - by some distance - the worst street in Manchester for parking fines. Thousands have been caught out with many criticising Manchester Council, which makes around £7m a year from parking fines across the borough

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05, 16 Sep 2026 Prison officers 'panicked' and didn't cut a hanged inmate's ligature or perform CPR for nearly three minutes, a coroner has said Arron Hamer died in hospital three days after being found hanged in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale . He was serving a controversial indeterminate public protection sentence , having been jailed aged 17 for two-and-a-half years for attempted robbery The 32-year-old was released in 2022, having spent 13 years in prison, but was recalled the following year after failing a drugs test. On June 18 last year he was found hanged in his cell and died in Royal Oldham Hospital three days later Now Manchester North senior coroner Joanne Kearsley has raised urgent concerns about his death. In a prevention of future deaths report sent to the prison and the chief coroner Ms Kearsley wrote: "Upon finding Mr Hamer the prison officers did not cut the ligature for nearly three "It was heard that they panicked and were visibly distressed on finding Mr Hamer. They had undertaken their basic life support training years ago on their initial prison officer training."

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:06, 16 Sep 2026 A notorious Manchester city centre street dubbed a council parking 'cash cow' has earned the town hall up to £724,000 in just three years even though there are only 29 bays, according to new figures obtained by the M For years St John Street in the city centre, home to a number of law chambers, was used by people heading into town to park for free after 8pm. All that changed in January 2024 when a new, single yellow line was painted along the road, prohibiting parking between 8pm and 8am In just three years, 22,607 penalty charge notices (PCNs) have been dished out to motorists caught out by the new arrangements, resulting in fines totalling £733,960, according to the new figures View 5 Images St John Street, Manchester (Image: Manchester Evening News) It means St John Street is - by some distance - the worst street in Manchester for parking fines. Thousands have been caught out with many criticising Manchester Council, which makes around £7m a year from parking fines across the borough

evidence_packet.title: 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes
evidence_packet.lead: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05
evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05, 16 Sep 2026 Prison officers 'panicked' and didn't cut a hanged inmate's ligature or perform CPR for nearly three minutes, a coroner has said Arron Hamer died in hospital three days after being found hanged in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale . He was serving a controversial indeterminate public protection sentence , having been jailed aged 17 for two-and-a-half years for attempted robbery The 32-year-old was released in 2022, having spent 13 years in prison, but was recalled the following year after failing a drugs test. On June 18 last year he was found hanged in his cell and died in Royal Oldham Hospital three days later Now Manchester North senior coroner Joanne Kearsley has raised urgent concerns about his death. In a prevention of future deaths report sent to the prison and the chief coroner Ms Kearsley wrote: "Upon finding Mr Hamer the prison officers did not cut the ligature for nearly three "It was heard that they panicked and were visibly distressed on finding Mr Hamer. They had undertaken their basic life support training years ago on their initial prison officer training."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Teenage football fan injured in city centre substance attack 'thought his eyes were on fire' The dad of the 16-year-old has spoken out after he had a substance 'squirted in his face' Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 19 The dad of a teenage football fan who had a substance 'squirted in his face' in a horrifying city centre attack says he fears he may lose the sight in one of his eyes Zak Hampton, 16, from Derbyshire, had travelled to Greater Manchester to watch his beloved Chesterfield play Oldham Athletic at Boundary Park on Saturday (September 12) After taking a tram back to Manchester city centre , he and the group of friends he was with became involved in what has been described by police as a 'verbal altercation' in Exchange Square Zak's dad, Lee, 42, said the group were singing football songs, but that the dispute was 'nothing to do with football.' evidence_packet.lead: Courts Why mum who shook baby girl to death following 'sadistic' abuse will not have jail term increased Omra Wali Jan suffered severe, traumatic brain injuries News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:56, 15 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Morsal Mohammed Naim, A mother who shook her baby
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Why mum who shook baby girl to death following 'sadistic' abuse will not have jail term increased Omra Wali Jan suffered severe, traumatic brain injuries News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:56, 15 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Morsal Mohammed Naim, A mother who shook her baby
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Why mum who shook baby girl to death following 'sadistic' abuse will not have jail term increased Omra Wali Jan suffered severe, traumatic brain injuries News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:56, 15 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Morsal Mohammed Naim, A mother who shook her baby girl to death after the tragic child was subjected to 'sadistic' abuse will not have her jail term increased Omra Wali Jan died in February 2024 after suffering having suffered severe, traumatic brain injuries caused by 'extremely forceful shaking' by her mother Morsal Mohammed Naim, following an incident the previous November. It came after Omra was beaten, burned with a lighter and bi Naim, 32, and her husband Firooz Wali Jan, 32, admitted child cruelty. Naim was accused of murdering Omra, but pleaded guilty to manslaughter. The pair have never explained themselves and the circumstances surrounding the child's death remain unclear Naim's barrister said the mum had been under 'extreme stress and strain'. Earlier this year, Naim and Wali Jan, who lived with Omra in Levenshulme, were sentenced at Manchester Crown Court. Naim, of no fixed address, was jailed for nine years. Wali Jan, of Seymour Grove, Old Traf Judge Mr Justice Turner told of what he described as 'sadistic behaviour' in the case, as well as 'multiple incidents of serious cruelty'. Following the sentencing, the Attorney General referred Naim's case to the Court of Appeal, arguing her sentence was 'unduly lenient'

evidence_packet.lead: They are warning that the expensive habit could lead to more crime and have floated the idea of giving crack pipes to users - similar to a needle exchange My colleague Damon Wilkinson has delved into the latest GM Trends drugs study and learnt how one drug user has fears of a 'cr
evidence_packet.summary: They are warning that the expensive habit could lead to more crime and have floated the idea of giving crack pipes to users - similar to a needle exchange My colleague Damon Wilkinson has delved into the latest GM Trends drugs study and learnt how one drug user has fears of a 'cr
evidence_packet.evidence_text: They are warning that the expensive habit could lead to more crime and have floated the idea of giving crack pipes to users - similar to a needle exchange My colleague Damon Wilkinson has delved into the latest GM Trends drugs study and learnt how one drug user has fears of a 'crack pandemic' emerging in the region. "Kids are being told it’s just cocaine on a pipe," the user said Damon has also spoken to rough sleepers on the streets of Manchester, including Michael, who says he is offered crack cocaine “five or six times a day”. "I don't do drugs, just a bit of cannabis, but people come up to me all the time asking if I want to buy crack," he said View 6 Images The popularity of crack cocaine is on the rise in Manchester (Image: Sunday Mail) He says he was recently robbed for just £7. "It's probably the crack, isn't it? People are running round crazy at the minute,” he said Michael’s experiences are indicative of a wider trend - with crack being sold for as little as £5 a rock on Greater Manchester's streets as it increasingly replaces heroin as the substance of choice for the city's rough sleepers, addicts and hard drug users

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Old Trafford site to be turned into 286 homes with just seven parking spaces Old Trafford residents fear an 'influx of on-street parking' Comments News Hannah Richardson 13:21, 15 Sep 2026 View Image CGI of the proposed Chester Road flats, in Almost 300 new homes could be built on the site of a disused petrol station and multi-storey car park in Old Trafford . The scheme, recommended to be approved by Trafford council’s planning committee next week, would see the existing structures demolished and two blocks of 286 fl One of the blocks would reach 16-storeys in height and contain 192 homes. The second would have 94 flats and be six-storeys at its tallest point But concerns have been raised by residents over a lack of parking provision on the land, which sits off Chester Road. Just seven vehicle spaces are proposed, which would be disabled spaces. Some 286 cycle spaces would also be offered Residents have branded this offering ‘insufficient’, saying there is already a ‘lack of parking’ in the area. They fear the development would bring an ‘influx of on-street parking’ which could cause obstruction and poor visibility on the surrounding roads They have also raised concerns about illegal parking and traffic congestion. Trafford council would typically expect around 425 parking spaces to be delivered for a scheme of this size

title: The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines

evidence_packet.title: The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhou
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhou
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The 29-space Manchester street that generated £733k in parking fines Motorists keep getting stung on St John Street which only has 29 parking bays View 5 Images A row of ticketed cars on St John Street including Alex Roberts' Sa Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:06, 16 Sep 2026 A notorious Manchester city centre street dubbed a council parking 'cash cow' has earned the town hall up to £724,000 in just three years even though there are only 29 bays, according to new figures obtained by the M For years St John Street in the city centre, home to a number of law chambers, was used by people heading into town to park for free after 8pm. All that changed in January 2024 when a new, single yellow line was painted along the road, prohibiting parking between 8pm and 8am In just three years, 22,607 penalty charge notices (PCNs) have been dished out to motorists caught out by the new arrangements, resulting in fines totalling £733,960, according to the new figures View 5 Images St John Street, Manchester (Image: Manchester Evening News) It means St John Street is - by some distance - the worst street in Manchester for parking fines. Thousands have been caught out with many criticising Manchester Council, which makes around £7m a year from parking fines across the borough

title: 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes

evidence_packet.title: 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes
evidence_packet.lead: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05
evidence_packet.summary: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Panicked' prison officers didn't cut hanged inmate's ligature for nearly three minutes Arron Hamer, who was serving a controversial IPP sentence, died in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale View 2 Images Arron Hamer died aged 32 News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:05, 16 Sep 2026 Prison officers 'panicked' and didn't cut a hanged inmate's ligature or perform CPR for nearly three minutes, a coroner has said Arron Hamer died in hospital three days after being found hanged in his cell at HMP Buckley Hall in Rochdale . He was serving a controversial indeterminate public protection sentence , having been jailed aged 17 for two-and-a-half years for attempted robbery The 32-year-old was released in 2022, having spent 13 years in prison, but was recalled the following year after failing a drugs test. On June 18 last year he was found hanged in his cell and died in Royal Oldham Hospital three days later Now Manchester North senior coroner Joanne Kearsley has raised urgent concerns about his death. In a prevention of future deaths report sent to the prison and the chief coroner Ms Kearsley wrote: "Upon finding Mr Hamer the prison officers did not cut the ligature for nearly three "It was heard that they panicked and were visibly distressed on finding Mr Hamer. They had undertaken their basic life support training years ago on their initial prison officer training."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Why mum who shook baby girl to death following 'sadistic' abuse will not have jail term increased Omra Wali Jan suffered severe, traumatic brain injuries News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:56, 15 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Morsal Mohammed Naim, A mother who shook her baby girl to death after the tragic child was subjected to 'sadistic' abuse will not have her jail term increased Omra Wali Jan died in February 2024 after suffering having suffered severe, traumatic brain injuries caused by 'extremely forceful shaking' by her mother Morsal Mohammed Naim, following an incident the previous November. It came after Omra was beaten, burned with a lighter and bi Naim, 32, and her husband Firooz Wali Jan, 32, admitted child cruelty. Naim was accused of murdering Omra, but pleaded guilty to manslaughter. The pair have never explained themselves and the circumstances surrounding the child's death remain unclear Naim's barrister said the mum had been under 'extreme stress and strain'. Earlier this year, Naim and Wali Jan, who lived with Omra in Levenshulme, were sentenced at Manchester Crown Court. Naim, of no fixed address, was jailed for nine years. Wali Jan, of Seymour Grove, Old Traf Judge Mr Justice Turner told of what he described as 'sadistic behaviour' in the case, as well as 'multiple incidents of serious cruelty'. Following the sentencing, the Attorney General referred Naim's case to the Court of Appeal, arguing her sentence was 'unduly lenient'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Woman who alleges she was raped and abused as child in Rochdale tells jury 'I'm not lying' Six men are on trial after three girls alleged they were abused News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 16:21, 15 Sep 2026 View Image The alleged abuse is sa A woman who alleges she was raped and sexually abused as a child in Rochdale told a jury ‘I’m not lying’ Six men are on trial at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester, accused of historic sexual offences. Tahir Rashid, 55; Mohammed Saleem, 47; Sucklane Shah, 47; Amjad Mahmood, 54; Iftaq Hussain, 46; and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face Girl A, as she is known, gave evidence in court and was cross-examined by Mr Rashid’s barrister. “I feel like I’m being called a liar, I’m not lying,” she said under questioning by Ayaz Qazi KC She and two other girls were ‘groomed', 'manipulated' and became 'sex slaves', often being forced to have sex ‘with multiple men on the same day, in filthy flats and houses’, prosecutors allege. The abuse of one, Girl C, allegedly began in the late 1980s, with the alleged ‘exploi Mr Mahmood is not present in the dock. The court has been told he is receiving treatment in a foreign hospital for a 'complex psychiatric illness' and 'through no fault of his own is unfit to stand trial.'

A few years ago, Elliott Street looked like many other struggling high streets: boarded-up shopfronts, empty windows, a town that felt left behind None of this change happened by accident. It happened because a local group, 'For Tyldesley CIC', took charge of a High Street Heritage Action Zone and brought empty buildings back into use – above the shops as well as within them That's the bit we overlook. When we talk about high street decline, we talk about what's at street level – the shops coming and going. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Greater Manchester Police officer of Chinese descent has spoken about his experience of being regularly racially abused on the job, including being spat at PC Michael Chiu spoke out after Greater Manchester Police Federation announced it was backing the ‘Protect The Protectors: Stop Racism Against Police’ campaign. The campaign aims to collect data on the scale of racial abuse against officers, raise awareness of what the police are PC Michael Chiu grew up in Northern Ireland; his family ran a Chinese takeaway and would regularly receive racist abuse. He said: “People would get really drunk and racially abuse you. At one point someone actually threw a firework at us. evidence_packet.summary: Ian Griffin, 57, was living in the summerhouse of his parent's home in Winwick, Warrington, when police were called and found his father Bernard Griffin with serious facial injuries, Liverpool Crown Court heard In May 2009, he had been sentenced to 20 years in Paris for killing K
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ian Griffin, 57, was living in the summerhouse of his parent's home in Winwick, Warrington, when police were called and found his father Bernard Griffin with serious facial injuries, Liverpool Crown Court heard In May 2009, he had been sentenced to 20 years in Paris for killing Kinga Legg, whose battered body was found in their room at the Bristol Hotel, but was released in 2016 after serving 22 months following an appeal on medical grounds The 57-year-old has been jailed for five years for causing grievous bodily harm and threatening to damage property Part of the attack, which was believed to have lasted between 30 minutes and an hour, was filmed by Griffin on his mother's phone It showed the defendant threatening his father to make him sign a note promising him to give 50% of his estate to his mother, Janet Griffin Bodyworn footage showed his father, then 83, with blood over his face and clothing

evidence_packet.summary: The skies over Manchester will light up once again as firework night celebrations are set to return with displays in Manchester parks this year bringing the city’s communities together
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The skies over Manchester will light up once again as firework night celebrations are set to return with displays in Manchester parks this year bringing the city’s communities together On Saturday 7 November, free family-friendly fireworks events at Wythenshawe Park, Heaton Park and Platt Fields Park will feature both a reduced-noise, low-impact display at 5pm for families and SEND audiences and a main fireworks display at 8pm, with accessibility and inclusivit Each of the three parks will host lantern making workshops in the weeks leading up to the events, with family-friendly lantern parades taking place ahead of the 8pm firework shows. Additional entertainment will be announced for each park in the coming weeks Major fireworks events had been paused in 2019 following the Covid-19 pandemic when funding challenges spurred a change of direction with the Council choosing to invest in a range of community focused events across the city’s parks through the autumn season – rather than the majo The good news is that these community focused events will still take place and are set to expand further in local parks this year, particularly in the run up to and during the October half term school holiday, with a mix of themed activities. Further details will be announced in With additional Council investment, the fireworks events on November 7 will be a grand finale to the community activities happening across the city

evidence_packet.summary: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount Offenders caught committing fly-tipping offences will now face a £1,000 fine, an increase from the current £700 penalty. Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. A total of 992 fines were issued for waste deposits in the same period The strategy supports the aims of the council's Our Manchester Strategy , which sets out a vision for cleaner, greener and better maintained neighbourhoods

evidence_packet.lead: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 8 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council
evidence_packet.summary: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 8 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 8 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council Fiona has enjoyed a distinguished career in local government law and public service, first qualifying as a solicitor in 1985 She has held range of senior leadership positions across local government, including roles at Stoke-on-Trent City Council, the London Borough of Brent, the Greater London Authority and the London Borough of Sutton Fiona joined Manchester City Council as City Solicitor in 2018, taking up a role that shares services with Salford City Council – an agreement that has been in place since 2012 to share resources and reduces costs across the two city councils A respected member of the legal services profession, Fiona served as President of the Manchester Law Society in 2025, representing and supporting the legal community across the region Fiona will stand down as City Solicitor in May 2027. The process to find her replacement is now underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Manchester cocktail bar, which has been named best in the UK, is opening in London’s Seven Dials Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Award-winning Manchester cocktail bar Schofield’s is heading to London, with brothers Joe and Daniel Schofield set to open their second venue in Covent Garden this November The pair have secured a site in Seven Dials, close to Shaftesbury Avenue and the West End, following almost three years of searching for a London home The venue will now undergo an eight-week fit-out ahead of a planned opening in early November Set across two floors, Schofield’s London will be larger than the original Manchester bar in both floorspace and capacity, with the two levels designed to offer different experiences “Upstairs will be for people to drop in for a quick drink, while downstairs guests will settle in for the night,” said Joe Schofield

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

Home to two of the most renowned clubs in British sport - Manchester United and Lancashire County Cricket Club , The Quays is the area to head for when wanting the best in football and cricket. Both have official sh Built in 2000 at the booming Salford Quays, this astonishing building is a shrine to all things art, with galleries, theatres, workshops, cafes and shops. It's worth a visit just to sit outside and admire the vision in metal and glass. But you'd be missing out on a whole world of Watersports The Salford Watersports Centre at The Quays is a unique sporting venue which is well placed and perfect for taking to the water. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.summary: JJ Gabriel rocked Man Utd by asking the club to leave and another academy graduate could get clarity on his future tonight
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Harry Amass Another Manchester United youngster might be about to find out where his future lies JJ Gabriel rocked Man Utd by asking the club to leave and another academy graduate could get clarity on his future tonight. Comments Sport opinion Tyrone Marshall Manch The build-up to Manchester United's Carabao Cup third-round tie with Brighton has been dominated by JJ Gabriel and his shock request to leave the club , but there are other youngsters pushing for involvement at Old Trafford tonight Shea Lacey should be handed a first start of the season and fellow academy graduates Harry Amass and Tyler Fletcher are both on the fringes of the first-team and could play in a game that has taken on greater significance this week The case of Amass is particularly interesting. He made his Champions League debut last week, playing the final 18 minutes against Sabah as United cruised to a 4-0 win, but he hasn't made a matchday squad in the Premier League so far With first-choice left-back Luke Shaw missing the weekend defeat to Manchester City , Michael Carrick again opted for Patrick Dorgu to start, with Noussair Mazraoui as cover, and despite the lack of options in that position, Amass isn't guaranteed to continue to get first-team mo Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!

evidence_packet.summary: ZLATA OGNEVICH — певица, автор песен, обладательница одного из самых мощных голосов Украины. Её вокал — это уникальное сочетание силы, нежности и глубокой эмоциональности, которое затрагивает самые потаённые струны души
evidence_packet.evidence_text: ZLATA OGNEVICH — певица, автор песен, обладательница одного из самых мощных голосов Украины. Её вокал — это уникальное сочетание силы, нежности и глубокой эмоциональности, которое затрагивает самые потаённые струны души 15 ноября 2026 года ZLATA OGNEVICH выступит в Лондоне на сцене легендарного клуба 229 В программе вечера — песни, которые уже стали знаковыми для многих: «Свет», «Аист», «Как мне быть», а также любимые хиты — «Кукушка», «Сладкая кара», «Танцевать». Прозвучат и популярные дуэты — «Без тебя» с Максимом Бородиным, «Буревиями» с SHUMEI, а также проникновенные сольные В последние годы ZLATA не только создавала новые песни — она была рядом с теми, кому её музыка была нужна больше всего. Её голос звучал для людей, потерявших дом, для тех, кто защищал свою страну, и для всех, кто искал свет в самые тёмные моменты Более ста выступлений в госпиталях, на волонтёрских и прифронтовых площадках, а также участие в благотворительных мероприятиях более чем в десяти странах мира сделали её голос одним из символов современной Украины ZLATA OGNEVICH — одна из самых ярких артисток современной украинской сцены. Её творчество сочетает безупречное вокальное мастерство, сценическую харизму и глубину настоящих эмоций

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events From Solo Thinker to Hive Mind: Why the Best Scaleup Teams Don't Look Like You From Solo Thinker to Hive Mind: Why the Best Scaleup Teams Don't Look Like You Official Chamber Post FREE GM Digital Security Hub (DiSH), Heron House, 47 Lloyd St, Manchester M2 5LE Wednesday 16 Every founder has a default hiring pattern: people who think fast the way you do, decide the way you do, work the way you do. It feels efficient. It feels safe. It is also the quiet reason so many scaleups hit a leadership ceiling exactly when they need more range in the room, no In this session, Barry McNeill and Mark Green (Co-founders, Work Progressive) take founders and senior operators through a live, physical experience of diversity of thought in action. To bring it to life, they will explore the dynamics of personal style and emotional intelligence This isn't a lecture on diversity of thought. It's a practical, occasionally uncomfortable look at your own hiring pattern, and a clear next step for building a leadership team or board that challenges you rather than agrees with you You'll leave with a simple model for talking about difference in your team, and one deliberate action to shift how you hire, delegate or listen over the next 90 days
